Unit: one representative genome per species. Boxes show the median and quartiles over genomes. The phylum tab comes first; subphylum, class and order are the other tabs. Each caption gives n and the share of genomes pooled in the grey "Other" group, read from the figure's data file.

**Definitions.** Each genome contributes one median, so large genomes do not dominate. The unit of each statistic differs:

- Gene length is per protein-coding gene (span of the gene model). Protein length is per protein in the protein table.
- CDS length, exons per gene, the share of genes with an intron and intron length are per transcript, over protein-coding transcripts. A gene with several isoforms counts once per isoform. Note that exon counts may include UTR exons.
- Coding fraction is the summed CDS length of all protein-coding transcripts divided by the genome length. Alternative isoforms add to the sum, so the value can be inflated in genomes with many isoforms.
- Intergenic distance comes from the intergenic-distance table and is not filtered to protein-coding genes.
- Genes per Mb counts distinct protein-coding genes.

## Group tests

Kruskal-Wallis and ANOVA across the groups of each level, one row per statistic. No multiple-testing correction is applied. Effect size is epsilon-squared from the Kruskal-Wallis test.

```{python}
table("T_anova")
```
